title: Held sources: field change, mutual cost and its sign

key_results.statement: Field operator with held sources: $C_f(g_1,g_2)=C_f+g_1\Phi_{x_1}+g_2\Phi_{x_2}$, the restriction of the total contract to a joint eigenspace of $(G_1,G_2)$; for $G_i,\Phi_{x_i}$ not multiples of $\mathbb 1$ invariant [I] as the sector operator $K_\alpha$, only its parametrisation by $(g_1,g_2)$ depends on the split.

For every field start and every body start in one joint eigenspace of $(G_1,G_2)$, the bodies stay in their start and the field evolves by $e^{-iC_f(g_1,g_2)\lambda}$, exactly for all $\lambda$; invariant [I] for $G_i,\Phi_{x_i}$ not multiples of $\mathbb 1$.

For a body start with components on several joint eigenspaces, (3.3) holds branch by branch and the field view is $\sum_g\lVert\beta_g\rVert^2\lvert\varphi_g(\lambda)\rangle\langle\varphi_g(\lambda)\rvert$, in general not pure; invariant [I] for $G_i,\Phi_{x_i}$ not multiples of $\mathbb 1$.

In the starts of (3.3) the cost is exactly $\langle C_f\rangle_\varphi+g_1\langle\Phi_{x_1}\rangle_\varphi+g_2\langle\Phi_{x_2}\rangle_\varphi$ and conserved; a field start independent of the sources carries no mutual term at any order; the cost of each state is invariant [I], and for $G_i,\Phi_{x_i}$ not multiples of $\mathbb 1$ the last statement has the invariant form of the zero mixed difference of the sector operators (3.26).

Response function of a non-degenerate eigenvector: $\chi_n(x,y)=\langle\varphi_n\vert\Phi_xQ_n\Phi_y+\Phi_yQ_n\Phi_x\vert\varphi_n\rangle$ with the reduced resolvent $Q_n$; real, symmetric, independent of phases, of the basis in other levels and of shifts $\Phi_x\to\Phi_x+c_x\mathbb 1$; class [F].

For non-degenerate $\varphi_n$ and $v<\Delta_n/2$: $E_n=e_n+\sum_i(g_i\bar\Phi_n(x_i)-\tfrac12g_i^2\chi_n(x_i,x_i))-g_1g_2\chi_n(x_1,x_2)+O(v^3/\Delta_n^2)$; $E_n$ is the invariant rank-$k$ eigenvalue of the sector operator [I], its decomposition is [F].
Second-order self terms $\Sigma_{n,i}=-\tfrac12g_i^2\chi_n(x_i,x_i)$ and mutual term $W_n=-g_1g_2\chi_n(x_1,x_2)$, relative to the expansion point $g=0$; class [F].

In the adapted eigenvector source $i$ changes $\langle\Phi_y\rangle$ by $\delta N^{(i)}_n(y)=-g_i\chi_n(y,x_i)$ up to $O(\lVert\Phi_y\rVert v^2/\Delta_n^2)$, reciprocally; from the unadapted start $\varphi_n$ the $\lambda$-average of $\langle\Phi_y\rangle$ equals this to the same order, while its cost stays (3.5); class [F].

For a level of multiplicity $d_\ell\ge2$ and $v<\Delta_n/2$, the $d_\ell$ branches are, up to $O(v^3/\Delta_n^2)$, the eigenvalues of $H_\ell(g)=\epsilon_\ell P_\ell+P_\ell VP_\ell-P_\ell VQ_\ell VP_\ell$; exact for a one-level field; class [F]; a vector $\psi$ of the level selects a branch (an eigenvector of $C_f(g)$ continuous at $g=0$ ending in $\psi$) if a subspace invariant under $C_f$, $\Phi_{x_1}$, $\Phi_{x_2}$ meets the level in the line of $\psi$, and this branch is analytic for $v<\Delta_n/2$, given by (3.7) with $\chi_\psi$ of (3.6), and [I] as an eigenvalue of $K_\alpha$ on that subspace; if $\hat g_1A_1+\hat g_2A_2$ has a simple spectrum for one direction, only joint eigenvectors of $A_1,A_2$ can select a branch, for $d_\ell=2$ with $[A_1,A_2]\neq0$ none does, and a joint eigenvector of commuting $A_1,A_2$ need not (control).

For $d_\ell=2$ with $[P_\ell\Phi_{x_1}P_\ell,P_\ell\Phi_{x_2}P_\ell]\neq0$, each branch $\epsilon_\ell+g_1\alpha_1+g_2\alpha_2\pm\lvert g_1\vec a_1+g_2\vec a_2\rvert+O(v^2/\Delta_n)$ depends on both sources at first order, non-additively and non-differentiably at $g=0$, so it has no mutual term $\propto g_1g_2$; control: commuting compressions, where single branches can be analytic with mutual terms of both signs while the level response vanishes; class [F].

The sum of the branches of a level is always analytic, with mutual term $-g_1g_2\chi^{(\ell)}(x_1,x_2)$ and level response $\chi^{(\ell)}(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}[P_\ell(\Phi_xQ_\ell\Phi_y+\Phi_yQ_\ell\Phi_x)]$; class [F]; the sum of the branches is the block sum of the ordered eigenvalues $E^{(k)}_\alpha$ over the $d_\ell$ ranks of the level, invariant [I], and the rank $\#\{m:e_m\le e_n\}$ is the same for every vector of the level and does not represent its branches.

For weights $p(e_n)$: $\chi_\rho(x,y)=\sum_{e_n<e_m}\frac{2(p_n-p_m)}{e_m-e_n}\operatorname{Re}(\langle\varphi_n\vert\Phi_x\vert\varphi_m\rangle\langle\varphi_m\vert\Phi_y\vert\varphi_n\rangle)$, second order, $v<\Delta_{\min}/2$, mixtures defined through spectral projectors; class [F].

Sum rule: $\sum_n\chi_n(x,y)=0$ for all $x,y$, and the same over the eigenvectors in any subspace invariant under $C_f$ and all $\Phi_x$; exactly, the sum over all branches has no mutual part at any order; class [F], the exact form is [I] as the sum rule of (3.26).

If $UC_fU^\dagger=-C_f$ and $U\Phi_xU^\dagger=\epsilon_x\Phi_x$: $E_{U\varphi_n}(g_1,g_2)=-E_n(-\epsilon_{x_1}g_1,-\epsilon_{x_2}g_2)$ and $W_{U\varphi_n}=-\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}W_n$; the ends of the spectrum have opposite mutual terms if $\epsilon_{x_1}=\epsilon_{x_2}$, equal ones otherwise; class [F], a shift of the $\Phi_x$ adds a term linear in $g$ to the first relation.

For weights non-increasing (non-decreasing) in $e$, $[\chi_\rho(x,y)]$ is positive (negative) semidefinite, the self terms are $\le0$ ($\ge0$) and $W_\rho^2\le4\Sigma_{\rho,1}\Sigma_{\rho,2}$, second order; the bound can fail for interior eigenvectors; class [F].

$\chi_\rho(x_1,x_2)=\sum_{k<L}(p_k-p_{k+1})S_k$; $W_\rho$ has one weak sign for all non-increasing mixtures iff the partial sums $S_1,\dots,S_{L-1}$ have one weak sign, and non-decreasing mixtures then have the opposite sign; the ordering alone does not fix the sign; class [F].

A non-degenerate eigenvector sharp at $x$ has $\chi_n(x,\cdot)=0$; if sharp at $x_1$ and $x_2$, $E_n=e_n+g_1N(x_1)+g_2N(x_2)$ exactly and the field changes only by a phase; $\chi_n\equiv0$ if sharp at all $x$; for $G_i,\Phi_{x_i}$ not multiples of $\mathbb 1$ the exact statements at $x_1,x_2$ are invariant [I], the rest [F]; if $G_i$ or $\Phi_{x_i}$ is a multiple of $\mathbb 1$, sharpness at $x_i$ and the response relative to the listed $C_f$ are statements in the stated split.

A field state that stays sharp at $x_1$ and $x_2$ along its evolution is changed by the sources only by the phase $e^{-i(g_1N_1+g_2N_2)\lambda}$, for all $\lambda$: a field state cannot stay sharp at the places of both bodies and respond to them; invariant [I] for $G_i,\Phi_{x_i}$ not multiples of $\mathbb 1$, otherwise a statement in the stated split (control: $G_i=\mathbb 1$, $C_f=\Phi_{x_i}=\sigma_3$ rewritten as $C_f'=3\sigma_3-2\sigma_1$, $\Phi'_{x_i}=\sigma_1$).

At second order $W=g_2\delta N^{(1)}(x_2)=g_1\delta N^{(2)}(x_1)$ and $\Sigma_i=\tfrac12g_i\delta N^{(i)}(x_i)$, identities between numbers in which the relative factor $\tfrac12$ counts diagonal and off-diagonal terms of the quadratic form; in the adapted eigenvector the pair terms contain the full fields of both sources, second-order part $2(\Sigma_{n,1}+\Sigma_{n,2}+W_n)$, the field term takes back half of it, and $\partial E_n/\partial g_i$ contains $\delta N^{(1)}_n(x_i)+\delta N^{(2)}_n(x_i)$ without a factor $\tfrac12$; what a held body feels is not defined by these identities; for an extreme non-degenerate eigenvector $\chi_n(x_i,x_i)=0$ iff it is sharp at $x_i$, and then $W_n=0$; class [F].

Three-place field $C_f=\omega(\lvert2\rangle\langle2\rvert-\lvert0\rangle\langle0\rvert)$, $\Phi_{x_{1,2}}=\lvert0\rangle\langle1\rvert\pm\lvert2\rangle\langle1\rvert+\text{h.c.}$: the interior eigenvector has zero self terms and mutual term $4g_1g_2/\omega$; a statement in the stated split.

For every field and $x_1\neq x_2$, at second order, either all level responses $\chi^{(\ell)}(x_1,x_2)$ vanish or both signs occur among the levels: $C_f$ and the $\Phi_x$ alone fix the sign of the mutual cost of like sources in no other case, and in that case only for non-degenerate eigenvectors and level sums; the state fixes the rest; class [F], the exact alternative for $\mathcal W_k$ in (3.26) is [I].

Three-place chain with $\Phi_x=\lvert x\rangle\langle x\rvert$: $\chi_3=-\chi_1$, $\chi_2=0$; the mutual part of like sources is $W=2u,3u$ (neighbouring, end places) in the lowest and $-2u,-3u$ in the highest eigenvector, $u=g_1g_2/(16\sqrt2t)$; sign and neighbour-minus-end difference of $W$ reverse; class [F], the same values hold for $\mathcal W_k$ with $(g_1-g_1')(g_2-g_2')$ in place of $g_1g_2$.

Three-place chain, lowest (upper sign) and highest (lower sign) eigenvector, $v<t/\sqrt2$: $E_n(1,2)-E_n(1,3)=g_2/4\pm g_2(g_2-2g_1)/(32\sqrt2t)+O(\lvert g_2\rvert v^2/t^2)$; for $g_2\neq0$ and small $v/t$ it has the sign of $g_2$ in both states, so the total cost does not reverse its preference between neighbouring and end place; invariant [I].

Replacements: $G_i\otimes\Phi_{x_i}=(a_iG_i+c_i)\otimes(\Phi_{x_i}-d_i)/a_i+d_iG_i\otimes\mathbb 1-c_i\mathbb 1\otimes(\Phi_{x_i}-d_i)/a_i$; for $G_i,\Phi_{x_i}$ not multiples of $\mathbb 1$ these are all writings of $C$ in the form of the setting, up to constants; $c_i=0$ keeps the decomposition of Steps 2–8 up to factors, $c_i\neq0$ moves the expansion point to $g_i=-c_i/a_i$ and changes it.

In one configuration the sectors, the sector operators $K_\alpha$ and their ordered eigenvalues $E^{(k)}_\alpha$ are fixed by $C$; exactly $K_{g_1g_2}-K_{g_1'g_2}-K_{g_1g_2'}+K_{g_1'g_2'}=0$, and the mutual cost of the change of both sources $\mathcal W_k$ satisfies $\sum_k\mathcal W_k=0$, so either all $\mathcal W_k$ vanish or both signs occur; invariant [I].

If (3.7) applies at the four sectors: $\mathcal W_k=-(g_1-g_1')(g_2-g_2')\chi_n(x_1,x_2)+O(v^3/\Delta_n^2)$, $k$ the rank of the non-degenerate $e_n$, in every split where this holds; for a degenerate level the sum of $\mathcal W_k$ over its block of $d_\ell$ ranks is the same with $\chi^{(\ell)}(x_1,x_2)$; the left side is invariant [I], and whether two changes are like is a convention in one configuration.

For the configurations with $\lvert X_f\rvert\ge3$, some $\Phi_x\neq\Phi_{x'}$ and $G_i$ not multiples of $\mathbb 1$, the invariant differences $C(x,y)-C(x',y)=G_1\otimes\mathbb 1\otimes(\Phi_x-\Phi_{x'})$ and $C(y,x)-C(y,x')=\mathbb 1\otimes G_2\otimes(\Phi_x-\Phi_{x'})$ fix $G_1,G_2$, zeros included, up to one common factor; the [F] results are then invariant under every replacement that is the same in all configurations, and total costs and their differences between configurations are invariant [I].

definitions.name: branch selected by a vector of a degenerate level
ordered eigenvalues of a sector operator
mutual cost of the change of both sources
invariance classes [I] (one configuration; for sectors and sharpness with G_i and the Φ at x_i not multiples of the identity) and [F] (family of configurations)
gap of the level of an eigenvector

open_issues: No relaxation (A11): what brings the field into an adapted state is open; in unadapted starts the cost has no mutual term (3.5).
Dependence on distance, whether the mutual term vanishes for far-apart sources, and hence which reading of the sign applies, belong to 04-profile.

For degenerate levels the level sums are always analytic; single branches may or may not be (Step 3); for branches not selected by an invariant subspace (Step 3, item 4) no general statement on their mutual terms is derived; orders above the second are not treated except in the exact results.
Mixtures are realised through an added object without contracts, an extension of the setting.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of every term of (3.7), and g_2 = 0 gives the one-source expansion

Two-place field: exact eigenvalues reproduce self and mutual terms of (3.7), the sum rule (3.14), the end relation (3.15), equality in (3.16) and the mixed sector difference (3.27); the common shift left by the two-place family changes C_f only by a constant
Φ_x commuting with C_f: χ_n = 0 and (3.7) equals the exact eigenvalue, as in (3.18)
